name: Kermit Green
lede: Kermit Green is a bright yellow-green crowd-named for Kermit the Frog in a 2010 online color survey, and it is almost absent from our painting archive.

sections.title: A Muppet's green
sections.body:
Kermit Green comes from the 2010 xkcd color survey, in which thousands of online respondents typed a name for each of a long series of randomly generated colors [1]. The name itself is simple: respondents matched the swatch to the skin of Kermit the Frog, the Muppet performed and voiced by Jim Henson since 1955 [1]. Our color graph records the origin plainly, as a color named for a person, Kermit [1].

The color graph puts Kermit Green almost on top of [[leaf-green]], 2.6 units away, and close to [[kelly-green]] at 3.2 units [1]. [[kelly-green|Kelly green]]'s own entry lists Kermit Green among its informal aliases, so the two crowd names describe nearly the same patch of yellow-green [1]. [[grass|Grass]] and [[nasty-green|Nasty Green]] sit a little further out, at 3.4 and 4.3 units [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings holds exactly one match for this color, as photographed, which makes it rarer than 86 percent of our named colors [2]. A bright, saturated internet-survey green like this has no pigment or dye history behind it, so painters had no reason to reach for anything so vivid [2]. The one match is a computed color distance, not a pigment identification [2].
